reader_question: Where did each 2024 presidential nominee’s joint fundraising committees send what they raised?
grade_line: Documented: the committees’ reports to the Federal Election Commission
title: In the 2024 cycle, Kamala D. Harris’s three joint fundraising committees sent $955.9 million to 54 other committees, and Donald J. Trump’s four sent $679.8 million to 56.
measure_line: Dollars each 2024 presidential nominee’s joint fundraising committees transferred to other committees (line 22 of their reports), 2023 to 2024 election cycle, not adjusted for inflation; a link’s width is its dollars, on one scale for both
source_line: Source: Federal Election Commission, itemized Schedule B transfers and refunds to other committees (lines 22 and 28C) of the seven committees the FEC designates joint fundraising committees that paid the Democratic or the Republican presidential campaign committee, and those committees’ Statements of Organization (Form 1), 2023 to 2024 cycle, United States. Retrieved November 12 and 13, 2026. Names and the dates they changed from Form 1; committees named as their payer wrote them before the November 5, 2024 election.
notes: Each party’s bar holds every committee the Federal Election Commission designates a joint fundraising committee that paid the party’s presidential campaign committee in the cycle: for the Democratic campaign, the Harris Victory Fund, the Harris Action Fund and the Harris Baldwin Victory Fund; for the Republican campaign, the Trump National Committee JFC, the Trump Save America Joint Fundraising Committee, the Trump 47 Committee and the Trump Bilirakis Victory Fund. The table gives each fund’s transfers.

On July 21, 2024, the Democratic campaign committee and its three funds filed new names: Biden for President became Harris for President, and each Biden fund a Harris fund. Before that day the three funds sent the campaign $161.4 million, the Democratic National Committee $85.8 million, 50 state party committees $68.1 million and one other committee $29,350; from that day on, $372.2 million, $155.1 million, $113.3 million to 51 and $9,290. The Republican campaign kept one candidate through the cycle, so its funds are not split; the Trump 47 Committee was named 2024 RNC Victory until March 14, 2024, and the campaign committee took the name Never Surrender, Inc. on November 12, 2024.

A joint fundraising committee raises money for several committees at once and splits it among them by agreement, so a transfer passes on money raised for the committee that gets it, and the agreement that formed a fund sets how many committees it pays.

The Democratic funds paid the state party committees of the 50 states and the District of Columbia, and the Republican funds those of 48 states, the District of Columbia and Guam; a committee two funds paid counts once. The download lists each with its transfers.

The chart draws transfers, line 22 of each committee’s reports, where a joint fundraising committee reports the shares it passes on. On the same reports, the Democratic funds also paid committees drawn here $27.3 million for operating expenses (line 21B) and the Republican funds $12.7 million, which the chart leaves out. The Democratic funds refunded $81,000 to two committees that had given to them, and the Republican funds $4,000 to four (line 28C); the table sets the refunds apart.
alt: Two senders side by side, one bar for the joint fundraising committees that paid each party’s presidential campaign, with links to bars for the committees they transferred money to, every bar as tall and every link as wide as its dollars on one scale. The three that paid the Democratic campaign, whose candidate was Joseph R. Biden Jr. until July 21, 2024, then Kamala D. Harris, sent $533.7 million to the campaign, $240.8 million to the Democratic National Committee, $181.4 million to 51 state party committees and $38,640 to one other committee, $955.9 million in all. The four that paid the Republican campaign, whose candidate was Donald J. Trump, sent $407.8 million to the campaign, $163.8 million to the Republican National Committee, $69.9 million to 50 state party committees and $38.3 million to four other committees, $679.8 million in all.
chart_notes: The chart draws both nominees’ committees alike, in one ink, on one scale: each bar is as tall as the dollars it sent or received, and each link as wide as the dollars it carried; a link under $4 million shows as a hairline.

notes_internal: Maker B, round 3. Data plan row 94 with change 8, rule 14.104. Data lead ruling (a): no named mark, both committees as a set; (b): both drawn alike, side by side from 680 px (one under the other below, each source's words heading its block under 420 px); every node edge and link in the party-mark ink (money spent to elect a candidate, Rule 14.6's list), node words in the text's ink; one linear unit for both, $4 million a pixel, with a key of three widths; Harris's 51 state party committees fold into one node and the table lists each.
